title: The sole nonzero differential under the explicit finite dual terms
statement: For any small site, sheaf R of commutative rings, global unit section a, and m >= 0, let c_m^q be the explicit isomorphisms of [def-pur-principal-koszul-dual-terms]. Then c_m^(-1) followed by the strict dual singleton differential from degree -1 to 0 equals the principal cone differential followed by c_m^0. This is an equality of morphisms between the actual term objects, without a tensor coefficient complex, derived category, inverse-limit functor, or assertion about other degrees.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, proof of lemma-derived-completion-koszul, identification of the dual positive Koszul complex with the negative Koszul complex; singleton calculation in the parent proof step 1.

proof.text: Remove the right tensor unit by its chain isomorphism. Project the Hom differential to source degrees 1 and 0. Its sign is -(-1)^(-1)=+1, giving precomposition by a^(m+1). Under rank-one evaluation at one this is multiplication by a^(m+1), since a^(m+1)r=r a^(m+1). The negative mapping-cone differential is its defining single chain map in its off-diagonal entry and all remaining matrix entries vanish. Induction identifies endoPow with categorical powers. Conjugate with the explicitly constructed term isomorphisms. These formulas remain valid for zero or invertible a, the zero ring and empty sites.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteDualTerm_nonzero_differential (m : ℕ) :
    (finiteDualTerm R a m (-1)).hom ≫
        ((ringedKoszulDualTower R 1
          (fun _ ↦ ⟨a.val, a.property⟩)).obj (op m)).d (-1) 0 =
      (principalKoszul R a m).d (-1) 0 ≫
        (finiteDualTerm R a m 0).hom
